title: Build, files and tools
goal: Run the program; each command and option; where the data comes from; what each dictionary file holds; how to measure a change.

blocks.x: What lyk is

lyk is steno with explicit word boundaries: every stroke after a word's first carries a join key (`+`), so a stroke without it always starts a word. The program generates the dictionary (steno JSON) from phonetic rules, starting from Plover's and Lapwing's outlines and measured against them. Rust, rules as data. American English only. See [the join key](#/ref/join-key).
Main features

items: **Cost-based outlines.** A word's single-stroke outline comes from whichever source (a known brief, the phonetic rules, a brevity-ladder compression) costs least to type; it need not be derivable from the word's sound or spelling.
**One primary outline per word.** Its other one-stroke forms (a Plover brief, the phonetic full form) are added last, only in strokes no other word needed.
**Measured.** `!score` and `build --report` print cost and match-rate against Plover and Lapwing on the same words. Benchmark tables are in the repository README, checked by `score --check-readme`.

**A miss types its word.** A stroke or `+` run the dictionary lacks is read by the solver (a keymux plugin lyk ships) as the word its keys sound like; `resolve` and `lookup` print the same answer: see [the solver](#/ref/fallback).

blocks.x: Commands
Run each as `lyk COMMAND` once installed, or `cargo run --release -- COMMAND` in a checkout.

head: Command
What it does
rows: Download the data into `data/` (safe to re-run): pronunciations, frequencies, Monkeytype's English word lists (`wordlists/monkeytype-*.json`, for `practice`), Plover and Lapwing, and the fifteen other theories as `dictionaries/theory-*.json` (see [other theories' briefs](#/ref/collisions)).
Show the version and the folders in use (data, out, dictionary, deploy target), the rule that chose each, and whether it exists (see [install and paths](#/ref/build-and-files/install-and-paths)).
How often the rules match Plover or Lapwing.
Check that the README's benchmark tables still match.
Rewrite any stale README table in place.

Briefs plus rules produce `out/lyk/02-lyk-*.json` (see [the files](#/ref/build-and-files/the-dictionary-files)) and print what was written: the total and one line per file, `(unchanged)` on a file whose bytes did not change. One extra warning line only when a word is stranded on a worse outline than its own plain reading. See [build output](#/ref/build-and-files/build-output).

`!build`, copied straight into keymux's live config with the reserved stroke tables and the solver plugin, and without the backups, which the solver replaces (see [the solver](#/ref/fallback/no-backups-in-keymux)). Default destination `~/.config/keymux/steno/lyk`; override with `--to`. Checked before it is written, and kept for one deploy: see [deploy checks](#/ref/build-and-files/deploy-checks-and-rollback). `--no-validate`, `--strict-validate` and `--rollback` change that.

Which rules wrote a word, next to Plover and Lapwing. Example: `explain moon`. With no word, the interactive session (see [the interactive session](#/ref/build-and-files/the-interactive-session)); Enter leaves the answer on screen and explains the line.

A word's family (`build`, `builds`, `building`...): each one's outline and its stem-plus-ending entry. With no word, the interactive session; Enter leaves the answer on screen and shows the family of the line (it generates the dictionary the first time). `--report` prints the numbers for the whole dictionary instead.

Every way to write a word as joined strokes, and what became of each. Example: `paths complete`. With no word, the interactive session; Enter leaves the answer on screen and shows the paths of the line (it generates the dictionary the first time).
Where the rules differ from Plover or Lapwing, for words of N syllables ranked after R. Example: `mismatches --syllables 2 --after 500`.
Which keys Plover and Lapwing use for each sound group, counting where they agree. Most rules were found this way.

Everything `build` leaves out by default: entries per source, words the rules could not place (with the commonest), backup entries skipped as collisions, words still contested after peeling, phrase and extra counts, stranded words, what a word costs next to Plover and Lapwing (strokes and keys), keys by frequency band, the commonest words on a star because another word holds their outline, and the words that cost the most extra keys over Plover.
Add a third dictionary to the cost tables of `build --report`. Example: `build --report --against magnum.rtf`.

A random quote, stroked in lyk next to Plover and Lapwing, a word that is not an entry composed from entries (see [how these commands answer](#/ref/build-and-files/how-quote-lookup-and-resolve-answer)).

A word, a phrase (its own entry first when it has one, then word by word: `lookup "to the"` shows the phrase `TOTD`, then *to* and *the*), or (all capitals) a stroke, answered from the built dictionary in lyk, Plover and Lapwing side by side. Example: `lookup "everybody's"`. A single word of two letters or more also finds every entry that is not a word, in lyk's column only, right after the word's best outline (at most eight rows): the suffixes, the keymux commands, the punctuation marks, the fingerspelled letters and OS shortcuts, and any dictionary entry whose text has a brace or other mark. A query matches an entry by its exact text (`{^}ing`, ignoring case), by its text without the `{`, `}`, `^` and `#` marks (`{^ing}`, `^ing` and `ing` all find `{^}ing` `[[+*G]]`, `up` finds `{#Up}`), or, from three characters, by a part of it, in that order: `lookup tape` shows `{:tape:toggle}` `[[PHRO*T]]` and `{:tape:clear}` `[[PHRO*TZ]]`, `lookup overlay` the three overlay controls, `lookup keyboard` the diagram toggle, `lookup control` the Control shortcuts. A query that is an entry's own text is not reported as a missing word. A command is shown without `{:firstup}` (or `{:firstup:except=KEYS}`) and `{:transparent}`, which say how it repeats or joins, not what it does. Keymux's live lookup does the same. With nothing after it, the interactive session: type, and the answer follows every key. `keys` is the same command under keymux's name. See [the interactive session](#/ref/build-and-files/the-interactive-session). **Every outline in lyk's column types the word in keymux**: a deployed entry, or (dim, under a note) a backup the solver reads as exactly that word; a backup it reads as another word is not listed, and a backup never stands for a word that has an entry (see [what lookup guarantees](#/ref/fallback/what-lookup-guarantees)).

Check that every outline `lookup` lists types its word in keymux: a deployed entry (the files `deploy` ships), else the solver reading it. Counts the listed outlines by how they were listed and what they type, with samples of any that do not, and fails on one. The default is a sample; `--full` is every word, phrase and name. `cargo test` runs a smaller sample. See [what lookup guarantees](#/ref/fallback/what-lookup-guarantees).

`lookup` with every query read as a stroke (lowercase is read as capitals), as keymux's `steno stroke`: what the stroke types in lyk (the dictionary's word, or the solver's reading of a miss, [the solver](#/ref/fallback)), then the entries nearest to it. Example: `resolve STKPW`. Use `--` before a run that starts with `-` or `~`: `resolve -- "-T/+-D"`. With no stroke, the interactive session.
`mistakes [--last N] [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--min-errors N] [--min-attempts N] [--top N] [--json] [--drill [--words N] [--out FILE]] [--tape FILE]`

A report on the keymux steno tape (default `~/.local/state/keymux/steno-tape.txt`), run once on demand: it reads the tape read-only and exits (nothing runs while typing, nothing is cached). Each stroke undone by `*` (or a `?` miss) is paired with the stroke struck next within 15 seconds, and counted as a mistake only when the two are a near-miss: one key added or missing, two keys added or missing, a neighbour key, the other hand's twin key (`S`/`-S`, `T`/`-T`, `P`/`-P`, `R`/`-R`) or a distant key swapped in. The same stroke again, another outline for the same text, a different word and two strokes retyped in the other order are counted apart, not as mistakes. The report lists the near-miss kinds; the words with the most mistakes and by error rate (mistakes over attempts, attempts being strokes that stayed typed plus mistakes); strokes by error rate; keys, fingers, rows and hands; the keys confused for each other; the commonest struck-to-intended pairs; and mistakes per day with the first and second half of the days compared. A row needs `--min-errors` mistakes (3) and, for a rate, `--min-attempts` attempts (20); a trend day needs 300 strokes. Keyboard-typed lines are never read, and only ordinary dictionary words are printed. The tape has only a time of day: a new day starts where the clock goes back and the last day is dated from the file's modification time, so `--last N` (the last N days with typing) is exact and `--since` approximate. `--json` prints the report as JSON. `--drill` writes `out/mistakes/drills.json` (or `--out`): the commonest mistakes weighted by error rate times how often the word is typed, each with its outline and a watch-out note naming the slip (`you often add -T`), plus the confusable word pairs. It also writes `monkeytype-drill.txt` beside it (`--words N`, default 150): the words only, ten a line, a confusable partner every fourth word, for Monkeytype's Custom text (Custom, Change, paste or import the file). Both files are gitignored and are never committed. Load the drills on the site's Practice page under *My drills* (a file picker, kept in the browser; or write them to `site/local/my-drills.json`, which the page loads by itself on a local server).
Score a stroke or a word's built outline finger by finger. With nothing after it, the interactive session; Enter leaves the answer on screen and scores the line.

`practice [--source S] [--new-per-session N] [--learning-cap N] [--gate PERCENT] [--wordlist monkeytype|lyk|both] [--monkeytype-weight X] [--deep] [--no-adapt] [--tape FILE] [--file PATH] [--rank MIN-MAX|--bands A-B,C-D] [--count N|--time SECS] [--seed N] [--weighted] [--no-repeat] [--lowercase-only] [--min-len N] [--max-len N] [--names] [--stop-on-error] [--requeue] [--quiet] [--outlines] [--no-save] [--dict DIR]`, `practice --history`

A typing drill in the terminal: a raw word feed, no outlines, keyboard or hints. The steno machine types the words through keymux as ordinary characters, so it reads plain key presses (a `*` undo arrives as backspaces). Space or Enter commits a word; a wrong word is an error and the feed moves on (`--stop-on-error`: it must be right first); Backspace deletes, and backspacing over the space reopens the word before; Ctrl-Backspace or Ctrl-W deletes a word; Esc or Ctrl-C quit at once at any time, with no results screen: the words typed so far are printed and saved as an incomplete run (nothing is printed or saved if no word was typed). `q` is an ordinary letter during a test. Tab restarts the test at any time, during a test or on the results screen: a fresh feed with the same options and a new random seed (with `--seed N` the seed goes up by 1 on each restart, so the feeds differ and stay reproducible), the timer and counters reset, and an abandoned test is not saved to the history. The clock starts at the first character typed after a start or restart; until then the live line reads `wpm 0`. The live line above the feed (`wpm 84   acc 97%   12/25   0:09`: words done out of the count and the time so far; in a `--time` run the words done and the time left) redraws about four times a second with no key pressed, so the time runs on and the speed falls. Under the feed a dim hint reads `tab restart  esc quit`. On the results screen Tab or Enter starts another test and `q`, Esc or Ctrl-C quit; Esc and Ctrl-C act at once, while for 0.7 s after the screen appears (and after each key it swallows) letters, Tab and Enter are ignored so keys still arriving from the run cannot restart or dismiss it, and afterwards they act at once. After quitting, the last results are printed into the terminal. `--source`: `adaptive` (the default: your own vocabulary, see [the adaptive vocabulary](#/ref/build-and-files/the-adaptive-vocabulary)), `common` (the commonest plain words of the subtitle counts, names left out unless `--names`; `--rank 1-1000` is the default, `--bands 1-200,201-1000` takes several bands, and `--weighted` draws each band equally often instead of each word), `mistakes` (the words of `lyk mistakes --drill`, a word once per copy in the set), `file` (`--file PATH`: the words of a text file), `phrases` (the phrasing grammar's phrases, `out/lyk/02-lyk-phrasing.json`, typed as their text), `quotes` (sentences from the books in `data/corpus`). `--count N` (default 25) or `--time SECS`; `--seed N` repeats a feed; `--no-repeat` uses each word once; `--lowercase-only`, `--min-len` and `--max-len` filter. Speed is correct characters over five per minute (raw counts every typed character); accuracy is by key press and by word; a word's time is since the word before it (a steno word arrives in one burst); consistency is 100 minus the spread of those times as a share of their mean. The results list the ten slowest words, the missed words with what was typed, and the stumbled words (right or wrong, but corrected before the word was committed, with how many corrections: a run of backspaces is one, and backspacing over the space to reopen the word before counts against that word); `--quiet` hides the live line and the hint; `--outlines` adds lyk's outline for each missed or slow word to the results (needs `lyk build`). Each finished test adds a line to `practice.jsonl` (`$XDG_STATE_HOME/lyk/` installed, `out/` in a checkout: time, source, words, speed, accuracy, errors, the missed feed words, the stumbled feed words); `--no-save` skips it, and `practice --history` prints the recent runs (with a `stb` column: words stumbled) and the trend. With the adaptive source a finished test (not one quit with Esc or restarted with Tab) also updates `vocab.json` (`--no-adapt` plays the feed without it) and a dim line under the results says what changed (`vocab  +2 new  1 mastered  1 stuck  3 due`); the feed is fixed at the start of a test (`--requeue` puts a missed or stumbled word back three words later in place of a base word, so the test keeps its length; see [the adaptive vocabulary](#/ref/build-and-files/the-adaptive-vocabulary)); with `--history` the last line is `N stuck words: lyk vocab stuck` when there are any. Needs a terminal on stdin and stdout.

`vocab [know WORD...|skip WORD...|forget WORD...|gate PERCENT|goal [TIER|N|clear]|reset --yes|seed|stuck|spread|clean [--dry-run]|unhide WORD...] [--json] [--wordlist L] [--monkeytype-weight X] [--names] [--deep]`

The adaptive vocabulary in `vocab.json`. With nothing after it: the vocabulary size (learning + review + retired words), the counts by status, the rank frontier (the next word the pool would introduce), the easy base's clean share against the gate (`filler clean x% (gate y%)`, with the last 3 tests' share) and the learning words' own clean share, the stumble rate over all attempts, the learning pool (stuck words marked), the reviews due now and next due with their dates, the recently mastered words, the words stumbled most in the last 7 days and the lapses (and, when no new word has come in for more than 14 days, why: the pool is full, or the easy base is under the gate); `--json` prints the same as JSON. `gate PERCENT` (0 to 100, or `default`) sets the gate for new words and keeps it in `vocab.json`; `--gate` on `practice` overrides it for one run. `know` and `skip` retire words (never shown, never introduced; kept on file); `forget` removes them from the file; `reset --yes` empties it (without `--yes` it only says what it would do) and does not read the history again; `seed [--tape FILE] [--dict DIR]` reads the history and the tape into the words not on file yet. `stuck [--json] [--tape FILE] [--dict DIR]` lists the stuck learning words, worst first: the last-10 clean count, the clean share and count of attempts since it entered learning, its stumbles, its best outline in the built dictionary with the key count and ergonomic cost (`lyk ergonomics`' weighted cost), and the ordinary word the tape most often typed when it was meant (counts only, no tape text); `--json` prints it as JSON. `spread` re-spreads the due days of reviews that are still as the seeding left them (never practised, missed, passed or lapsed) when more than 15 of them are due on one day, each into its level's window from today (level 1: 1 to 14 days, 2: 3 to 21, 3: 7 to 30, by a hash of the word, at most 15 due a day); it writes `vocab.json.bak` first and a second run changes nothing. `clean` removes from every status (learning, review, retired, new on file) each word that is not a practice word (see **Practice words** below) and records it in `hidden`, so it is never seeded or introduced again; it writes `vocab.json.bak` first, prints the counts by status and the first 30 words removed, and a second run removes nothing; `clean --dry-run` prints the same and writes nothing. `unhide WORD...` takes words off `hidden` (a word that still fails the predicate stays out of the feed, and the command says so). `know` and `skip` take any number of words. The plain summary also prints the tier table (see **Levels and the goal** below: tier, words, known, percent, the level marked); `--json` has `tiers`, `level` and `goal`. `goal` with nothing after it prints the goal and its bar; `goal TIER` sets it (`200`, `1k`, `5k`, `10k`, `25k`, `lyk`, `deep`, with or without a `monkeytype-` prefix, or a plain number of words such as `3000`), `goal clear` removes it; it is kept in `vocab.json` and an older file without one loads as no goal.

blocks.x: `--rules FILE` and `--briefs FILE` make a command use your own rules and briefs.
The adaptive vocabulary

`practice`'s default source builds each test from `vocab.json` (`$XDG_STATE_HOME/lyk/` installed, `out/` in a checkout, beside `practice.jsonl`): per word a status, attempts and hits, the last 10 results as marks, a speed average, day numbers (days since 1970-01-01), a review level, counts of promotions, lapses and stumbles (with the last 7 days of stumbles by day), the attempts typed in practice (all, and since it entered learning with how many were clean), whether it is stuck, the last 50 first attempts of review words and the last 3 tests' share of them (the easy base the gate reads), and the gate if one was set, the `hidden` words (removed by `clean`) and `filter_version` (the version of the practice-word predicate the file was last cleaned with; `lyk practice` cleans a file with a lower one once, writing `vocab.json.bak` first and printing a dim line `vocab cleaned: N words hidden (lyk vocab clean --dry-run to review)`); nothing typed that was not a feed word. A word is `new` (on file with past counts only, or not on file), `learning`, `review` or `retired`. Every constant is a field of `Config` in `src/practice/adaptive.rs`; `--new-per-session`, `--learning-cap` and `--gate` set three of them.

items: **The pool and its order.** The union of lyk's frequency list (filtered as `--source common`: plain words, no names unless `--names`) and Monkeytype's lists, each word once. A word in lyk's list ranks by that rank. A word only in a frequency-ordered Monkeytype list (`english`, `english_1k`, `english_5k`, `english_10k`) ranks by its position in the list times the list's scale (the median of lyk rank over list position for the words both have). A word in any of those four lists has its rank multiplied by `--monkeytype-weight` (0.7: met earlier than its rank says; 1 turns it off). After them come the words only in `english_25k`, then those only in `english_450k`; both files are unordered, so each tier is in a fixed scrambled order. Only practice words enter the pool (the next item); a lyk-only word is in the mixed pool only within rank 20,000 and only if Monkeytype's 450k dictionary has it. `--wordlist monkeytype` leaves lyk's list out, `--wordlist lyk` leaves Monkeytype's out and reads the whole frequency list on in chunks (the default is `both`). The first ~50,000 words are built when the command starts and the tiers are read only when the walk reaches them, so nothing is loaded early. By default the pool is about 35,000 words (about 24,700 in the head and 10,600 in the 25k tier); `--deep` adds the rest of the 450k dictionary (about 420,000 words in all).

**Practice words.** One predicate (`practice::words`) decides which words the pool, the seeding, `vocab clean` and the adaptive feed accept. A word qualifies when: (1) it is letters only, with an inner apostrophe only in a real contraction of a fixed list (`don't`, `can't`, `it's`, `I'm`, ...), two letters or more except `a` and `I`; (2) it is a contraction of that list, or in one of Monkeytype's `english`, `english_1k`, `english_5k`, `english_10k` or `english_25k` lists, or in the short list of ordinary spoken words those lists leave out (`ok`, the profanity of speech, `till`, `tv`), or within rank 20,000 of lyk's frequency list *and* in the 450k dictionary (written lowercase there, so capitalised names do not count) with four letters or more (three letters within rank 5,000); (3) it is not a morpheme fragment: no text of a suffix or prefix entry of lyk's rules (`rules/suffixes.toml`, `rules/morphemes.toml`, the family endings and prefixes) and none of a fixed list of fragments (`er`, `ed`, `ly`, `le`, `en`, `ent`, `st`, `ta`, `kon`, `eer`, `ing`, `ion`, `ism`, ...), unless it is also a word of Monkeytype's lists up to the 10k or of a short list (`age`, `less`, `over`, `or`); (4) it is not a vocal noise or an exclamation (the `no prose use` letter shapes: `ugh`, `hmm`, `zzz`, `ooh`); (5) it is not a name that Plover and Lapwing only write capitalised, unless `--names`. `--deep` lifts only the frequency limits of (2): any lowercase word of the 450k dictionary qualifies, and (1), (3), (4) and (5) still apply; a rare real word of the dictionary (not a name by those sources) can still show up there, and a rank alone never qualifies a word while the 450k list is downloaded. Without the Monkeytype lists the rank within 20,000 decides.

**A clean attempt.** An attempt is clean only when the word was committed right and no correction was made while it was open: no backspace or word delete that removed characters of it, and no backspacing over the space after the previous word to reopen it (a run of backspaces, such as a steno `*` over a whole word, is one stumble; a reopened word is a stumble of that word). A word committed right after a stumble is right but not clean, and counts as a miss everywhere below. A word refused by `--stop-on-error` is a miss; deleting the refused word is not a second one. The word is the first in pool order that is not learning, in review or retired. Each new word is in its first test twice.

**Mastery.** A learning word becomes `review`, level 1, when at least 9 of its last 10 attempts are clean and its speed average is within 1.5 times the median of the words that have one (not checked while fewer than 10 have). There is no day count: every attempt counts, a second copy of the word in the same test included, so a word is mastered the test its last 10 attempts reach 9 clean (at least 10 attempts on record, about 5 tests at 2 copies a test for a new word, 10 at one).

**Review.** Intervals by level 1 to 6: 1, 3, 7, 21, 60 and 180 days. A due review word passed (every attempt in the test clean) moves up a level and is due one interval later; at level 6 it stays. A miss moves it down one level (never below 1) and makes it due tomorrow; two misses in a row send it back to learning (when 10 words are already learning, it stays a level-1 review, the lapse counted). A review word not yet due does not move when passed.

**A test has exactly `--count` words** (25 by default). Learning words (new and stuck ones included) are at most 40% of it (10 of 25), in this order of priority: up to 2 stuck words (the longest unseen first), the new words twice each, the learning words that stumbled or missed in the last 2 tests (the most stumbles first), then the other learning words by recent error rate (a recent stumble adds weight, more for more stumbles); each once; then a second copy for the 3 with the highest recent error rate if room is left. Due reviews fill at most 30% (7 of 25), the longest overdue first. The rest is the easy base: reviews not yet due, drawn from the cleanest (lowest recent error rate, then the higher level, then the more typed). A vocabulary too small to fill a test (a fresh start with no tape) fills it with more due reviews and then repeats of the learning and new words (5 times each at most). Shuffled with `--seed`, no word twice in a row. A `--time` test repeats the rounds without adding new words.

**Within a test.** The feed is fixed when the test starts: exactly `--count` words, none replaced or added while you type (a stumbled or wrong word is drilled first in the next tests instead). With `--requeue` a word that stumbled or was committed wrong comes back 3 words later (not next to itself) *in place of* a later easy-base word, never a due review or a learning word, so the test keeps its length; a word is in a test at most twice, a returned copy included, and three times once it has been unclean twice; with no base word ahead it does not return. Backspacing over the space to reopen a word gives the base word back until it is committed again.

**Earning a new word.** The learning cap has a free slot (stuck words do not count) and the *easy base* is clean enough: the clean share of the first attempts of review words in tests (not the learning words, which are drilled every test and mostly unclean) over the last 50 such attempts is at least the gate (70%; `lyk vocab gate`), or the last 3 tests' easy base together reach it; with fewer than 20 on record it is not held against you. At most 2 new words a test. The gate default is below the typical clean rate of a review word (the tape median 74%) so an ordinary test passes.

**Stuck.** A learning word with at least 30 practice attempts since it entered learning (a seeded word counts attempts typed in `practice`, not the tape's), under 30% of them clean, and practised on at least 7 days (the day count includes the tape's days for a seeded word) is marked stuck: it leaves the learning cap, so a new word can be earned, and is drilled lightly (at most 2 stuck words in a test, the longest unseen first, once each). It stops being stuck when it is mastered (9 of the last 10 clean: a review) or has 9 of 10 clean while the cap has a free slot. `lyk vocab stuck` lists them; a word that stays stuck is probably an outline that does not suit your hands.

**Levels and the goal.** The pool is cut into tiers by the list a word first appears in, in this order: Monkeytype `english` (200 words), `english_1k`, `english_5k`, `english_10k`, `english_25k` (each tier holds only the practice words that no earlier list has: about 200, 808, 3,838, 4,676 and 20,480), then `lyk top 20k` (practice words of lyk's frequency list up to rank 20,000 that no Monkeytype list has: about 5,300), and with `--deep` the rest of the 450k dictionary. A word is *known* when it is in review or retired (learning counts 0; hidden words are left out). A tier is complete at 90% known, and your *level* is the first tier that is not complete (`lv1` is the first). The results screen shows `lv1  monkeytype 200  [█████░░░░░] 52%  104/200 known   next: monkeytype 1k`. A *goal* (`lyk vocab goal 1k`) adds a second, thin bar: the known share of every word in the tiers up to and including the goal tier (or of the first N words in tier order). New words still come in pool order (frequency rank, with Monkeytype's lists met earlier by `--monkeytype-weight`), not tier by tier, so the order and the tiers agree closely but not exactly.

**Retired.** `vocab know` and `vocab skip` retire any number of words: never shown, never introduced, kept on file so they are not introduced again. A word `vocab clean` removed is hidden instead: off the file and out of every later seeding.

**What updates it.** Only a test run to its end (the feed or the clock) counts; Esc, Ctrl-C and Tab leave `vocab.json` as it was. A word's time is the time since the word before it, as the results screen measures it (the first word of a test carries none). The day is the local calendar day.

**Seeding.** When `vocab.json` does not exist, the first adaptive run reads, once, the missed words of `practice.jsonl` and the steno tape's per-word counts (`lyk mistakes`' replay; ordinary words of the built dictionary that are also practice words (see above) only, and no word the tape typed by a continuation stroke (`+`: a suffix, a prefix or a fragment joined to the word before it); attempts, errors, distinct days and the last day are kept, no tape text): the thresholds are the typist's own, since steno corrections show as undos: the median error share over the words with 20 or more attempts (capped at 50%; the overall share when there are none) is the baseline. A word with 20 or more attempts at or below the median starts in review at level 1; at 20% wrong or less, level 2; among the 200 most typed and at 20% or less, level 3; due on a day inside its level's window counted from the seeding (level 1: 1 to 14 days out, level 2: 3 to 21, level 3: 7 to 30, picked by a hash of the word, at most 15 due a day), so the first reviews are not one wall. An existing `vocab.json` is not re-seeded; `vocab spread` re-spreads a wall. A word with 5 or more attempts above the median that is not in review starts in learning (the 10 with most errors). Every other word with a history is `new` with its counts, so it comes in pool order. No tape: it starts empty. The file records that it was seeded, so `reset` does not seed again; `vocab seed` adds words not yet on file, never a `hidden` one.

blocks.x: Install and paths

The binary is `lyk` (package `lyk-steno-theory`). Install it with `make install` (`PREFIX=/usr/local` by default, `DESTDIR` honoured; `make uninstall` removes it), with `makepkg -si` (the `PKGBUILD` builds the checkout you are in; optional dependencies: `keymux` for `deploy`, `python` for `tools/`, `nodejs` for `site/check.mjs`), or from a release tarball (`lyk-VERSION-ARCH.tar.gz`: the binary, README, LICENSE and NOTICE; lyk is GPL-3.0-or-later). The rules are compiled into the binary; nothing but the data below is read at run time. Then `lyk fetch`, `lyk build`, `lyk deploy`.

A checkout is the current folder when its `Cargo.toml` names `lyk-steno-theory` and it has `rules/`; then `data/` and `out/` are relative to it, as always. Under out: `lyk/` is the built dictionary (`build --out` and the `--dir`/`--dict` options default to it), `cache/` the lookup cache, `mistakes/` the tape reports. `lyk where` prints the version, the mode, every folder in use with the rule that chose it, and whether it exists. With no data, every command that needs it stops with a message pointing at `lyk fetch`. `deploy` writes `~/.config/keymux/steno/lyk` (`--to`) and needs `keymux` installed for validation. Environment: `LYK_VERSION` sets the version a build reports (release builds), `LYK_NO_STALE_NOTE=1` silences the stale note.

Two small files also land in `out/lyk/`, neither a dictionary, neither shipped by `!deploy`: `family.json` (which entries of `!words` are a family's shape, so a dictionary read back ranks them as the generator did) and `.built` (rewritten by every `!build`, even when no dictionary file changed, so its time says when the dictionary was last checked against the rules; holds only the source hash, see Version below).

items: The generator keeps exactly one word per outline: **no outline appears in two files**, so load order never changes what a stroke types. `!build` checks this.
Which file an entry goes in is decided in one place, `Role::of` in `src/output.rs`, from the entry's `Origin`.
The file name says the kind of outline: a `+` outline in `backups` is a fallback; the same word's primary is in `!words`.

keymux caches and reloads per file. A change moving only some entries rewrites only those files; `!build` compares bytes first, so an unchanged file is not rewritten and keymux has nothing to do for it.

blocks.x: How quote, lookup and resolve answer

These three read back the dictionary `!build` wrote to `out/lyk` instead of regenerating: a few seconds at most, not tens, with the same outline for every word (a test writes a build, reads it back and compares every word). If the stamp in `out/lyk` says other rules or another generator made it, a dim note says so (see Version below); `--rebuild` generates from scratch. With no built dictionary they generate. `lookup` and `resolve` also keep what they read in `out/cache/` (the gold dictionaries, the pronunciations, the read-back entries, the backups sorted by word), remade on the first lookup after the program or any source file changes; a lookup takes about a tenth of a second rather than two.

items: **A word that is not an entry is composed from entries.** `everybody's` is not a dictionary word, but `everybody` (`EFB`) is and `'s` is a standalone suffix stroke (`+-PBTS`): the answer is `EFB/+-PBTS`, two strokes, labelled `composed`. A word of two dictionary words (`noone`: `no` then `+one`) works the same way. Fewest strokes wins, then fewest keys, then fewest pieces; the rules' syllable-by-syllable reading is used only if it costs less; a tie goes to the pieces. It is listed only when the solver reads it as the word (else the rules' reading or the spelled form is).
**The join key is written out.** Every stroke after a word's first carries `+`, in the rules' own readings too, as in the dictionary files.

**Plover and Lapwing get the same treatment.** Where a theory has no entry for a word, `quote` and `lookup` compose one from that theory's own words and suffix strokes (`{^s}`, `{^'s}`, `{^ing}`), with its `{^}` stroke between two words (neither has a join key). A `-` in their column means they cannot write the word that way.
A composition needs both pieces to be dictionary words of at least two letters (or a suffix after the first piece): no stray letter is a "word".

blocks.x: The interactive session

`lookup` (alias `keys`), `resolve` (alias `stroke`), `explain`, `ergonomics`, `paths` and `family` take a word or a stroke and print their answer and exit. With **nothing** after the name, each opens the same session: a `›` prompt, and under it the answer for what is typed so far, redrawn in place on every key. It matches keymux's `steno lookup` / `keys` / `stroke` line for line (`src/answer.rs`, `src/view.rs` and `src/interactive.rs` mirror keymux's `steno/answer.rs`, `view.rs` and `interactive.rs`), except that keymux resolves its one engine setup and this shows all three theories. It reads the built dictionary in `out/lyk`: starts in a second or two, each key instant; `--rebuild` generates from scratch.

items: **The screen.** One prompt line (`› ` and your query), the answer under it, a dim line of hints at the end. It never switches screens, so what you keep stays in scrollback, and never grows past the terminal's height (a line `… N more lines` says what was cut). A burst of keys (a paste, a held Backspace) costs one search.

**The table.** Columns `word`, `lyk`, `plover`, `lapwing` (each outline column at least 12 wide, as in `quote`), and `keys` when shown. A word's first row has its best outline in each theory; each later row (word column blank) is another outline that types it, fewest strokes first, backups included: all of lyk's, Plover's and Lapwing's. `-` is a theory with no outline there. A single word of two letters or more is followed by up to eight longer words starting with it (dimmed; shortest first, then alphabetical), each with its best outline in the three theories.

**A word that is not an entry** is composed from entries when that takes no more strokes than the rules' reading, with a note under the table: `everybody's was not a whole entry - composed (lyk: everybody + 's; plover: everybody + 's; lapwing: everybody + 's)`, naming each theory that composed it. Otherwise lyk shows the rules' phonetic reading, or spelling mode for a word with no pronunciation, in quotes with a note (`has no dictionary entry - shown ...`). A word nothing can write shows `no stroke`. A real entry always wins.

**A stroke** (all capitals, or anything in `resolve`/`stroke`) shows what it types in quotes in the `word` column: the dictionary's word, the rules' reading with a note when it is not an entry, or `(no translation)`. Under it, dimmed, the nearest entries (same stroke count, fewest keys different). A stroke is lyk's alone, so this table has only the `lyk` column. A stroke the phrasing grammar writes (`SWRAB`, *I can be*) also gets the lines described in the next item.

**A phrase the phrasing grammar writes** (*I was*, *they wouldn't*) gets a row first, marked as the grammar's, then each word's rows, and two lines under the table naming its parts (`SWR starter (I) + E auxiliary (past) + -B verb (be)`): see [looking a phrase up](#/ref/phrases/looking-a-phrase-up).

**Totals.** Under the table: `keys (best outline of each word): N in S strokes` for lyk, then `keys (shared vocabulary only, fair comparison): lyk-vs-plover ... lyk-vs-lapwing ...` as `quote` prints it, counting only words both theories write. Completions and nearby entries are not counted.

**Colour, where the terminal has it** (`NO_COLOR` and a pipe turn it off): each key is coloured by keyboard part (green left hand, yellow vowels, red right hand, cyan `*`, `#` and the `+`/`~` marks), the `/` between strokes is dim, and keys one finger plays together (`T K`, `P W`, `H R`, `A O`, `E U`, `F R`, `P B`, `L G`, `T S`, `D Z`) are underlined as one run. Colour never changes the text.

**Keys.** Any character adds to the query (the stroke test is case-sensitive: capitals with no lowercase read as a stroke). Backspace, Ctrl-W, Ctrl-U delete a character, a word, the whole query. Tab shows or hides the `keys` column: the QWERTY keys that press lyk's outline, the join key `+` on `T` (the left index finger's inner column; `G` presses it too), the star on `Y` (the right index; `H` too), `S-` on `A` (`Q` too). Ctrl-F toggles best outline of each word only. Enter leaves and keeps the answer on screen (in `explain`, `ergonomics`, `paths` and `family` it then runs that command's report for the line; `family` and `paths` generate the dictionary the first time). Esc, Ctrl-C, Ctrl-D leave and clear the screen it used.
**Flags.** `--show-keys` starts with the keys column shown and `--fast` with only best outlines, on `lookup` and `keys`; `resolve`/`stroke` have neither.

**Bare or with an argument.** Bare opens the session (needs a terminal at both ends). With an argument the same table prints once, plain when piped. With input piped in and nothing after the name, one query is read per line, each answer printed followed by a blank line; an empty line or end of input stops it. A whitespace-only query prints `Nothing to look up`.

**Where it differs from keymux** (lyk has three theories and no keyboard config): a column per theory; the second totals line; the composed note names the theory; one `keys` column, for lyk; the keys column uses the default QWERTY layout and the author's `+` on `T`/`G` and star on `Y`/`H` instead of reading a keymux config; a stroke query fills lyk's column alone; lookups are on lowercased words (no capitalized entries); a word the dictionary lacks can be shown as the rules' reading, which keymux does not do.

The version is written nowhere: `build.rs` asks git when the program is compiled and bakes the answer into the binary, as keymux does. `lyk --version` (or `-V`) and the hidden `version` command (in no help or menu) print `lyk <version>`. `build` prints it as the first line of its output (also with `--report`).

Version printed
rows: Either, with uncommitted changes to tracked files
No version tag (there are none yet)
Cargo.toml's version and the short hash: `0.1.0+g0587d41`, `0.1.0+g0587d41.dirty`

blocks.x: Tags are read only when named `v` and a number (`git describe --match 'v[0-9]*'`); `LYK_VERSION=1.2.0` in the environment at compile time overrides everything. A plain `cargo build` or `cargo run` after a commit, checkout or edit to `src/`, `rules/` or `Cargo.toml` shows the new version without `cargo clean`; works inside a linked worktree.

**The stale check.** `build` writes `out/lyk/.built`: one line, `source=<hash>`, a content hash (computed by `build.rs` at compile time) of what decides the dictionary's bytes: every `.rs` file under `src/`, every file under `rules/`, `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` (relative names and contents). Docs, `site/`, the README, `docs/`, `plans/` and the git commit are not in it: a docs-only commit never makes `out/lyk` look stale; any change to rules or generator does. `lookup`, `resolve`, `explain`, `quote`, `ergonomics`, `paths` and `family` compare it with the running binary's hash when they read `out/lyk` back, and print one dim line on stderr if it differs: `note: out/lyk may not match this code: the rules or the generator changed after it was built; run build (or pass --rebuild)` (or `it was built before builds recorded the source they came from` for an older stamp). It prints once per run (the interactive session checks once at the start), never when stdout is not a terminal, never when either hash is `none` (no `src/` or `rules/` to hash). `--no-stale-check` or `LYK_NO_STALE_NOTE=1` silences it; `--rebuild` generates from scratch instead of reading `out/lyk`. `build` and `deploy` always generate, so never check. The version line (the git hash) is for `--version` and the `build` header only; it is not compared.
Build output

`!build` and `!deploy` are quiet: the version line, the `wrote N entries` line, one line per file (`(unchanged)` when nothing changed), and a `warning:` line only if a word is stranded on a worse outline. Diagnostics are `build --report`; the health conditions they showed are asserted by tests that stay silent unless one fails (`cargo test --release`; skipped with a message if `data/` is missing).

blocks.x: Building and deploying

`!deploy` replaces every generated file, then removes any `02-lyk-*.json` in the destination that this layout no longer writes. Files are sorted by outline and pretty-printed identically each time, so the same dictionary gives the same bytes.
Deploy checks and rollback

items: **Staged first.** Every file is written to `.lyk-staging/` beside the destination folder (a hidden sibling, so keymux does not read it), checked there, and only then moved into the live folder, one atomic rename per file. The live folder is not touched before the check passes.

**Validated.** The staged `.json` files go through `keymux steno validate --json` (the `keymux` first on `PATH`). Errors stop the deploy and nothing is written. Warnings are printed and the deploy continues; `--strict-validate` stops on them too. `--no-validate` skips the check.
**Summary.** One line of counts (errors, warnings, notes, files, entries), then the first 10 errors and warnings as severity, file, outline and message. `keymux steno validate` lists the rest.
**No validator.** With no `keymux` on `PATH`, or a validator that cannot run (its exit code 2) or prints no JSON, one `validate: skipped, ...` line says why and the deploy continues.

**Previous files.** Before the first rename, every file in the live folder is kept in `.lyk-previous/` beside it (hard links, so no copying; the folder holds one deploy and is replaced by the next). If the swap or the cleanup of old files fails, the live folder is restored from `.lyk-previous/` and the command fails.

**`deploy --rollback`** restores `.lyk-previous/` into the live folder (the files then there are replaced or removed) and does nothing else: no build, no check. It fails when there is no `.lyk-previous/`.

blocks.x: Analysis tools

Python 3, no dependencies, in `tools/`. Each tool reads the built dictionary in `out/lyk/` (run `cargo run --release -- build` first) and the data in `data/`, from wherever it is run. `lyk_out.py` is the shared loader, not a tool.

head: Tool
What it answers
rows: Who holds an outline (`TKO*BG` is *dock*, in `!words`), or every outline a word has, fastest first. Quote outlines that contain a star.
What a change did: per-file entry and word counts, the words only one build has, and every word whose fastest outline changed, commonest first, with counts for the top 1,000 / 5,000 / 20,000.
How many words of two syllables or more can be joined in, by frequency band: one-stroke share, joined share, stem-plus-ending share, joined ways in per word (see [ways to join](#/ref/ways-to-join)).
Words still on a bare `/+*` marker, by band, real words against names, and who holds the plain and starred stroke each real word wanted (see [collisions](#/ref/collisions)).

The phrasing grammar's tables as an independent spec: checks every stroke of `DIR/02-lyk-phrasing.json` (default `out/lyk`) against it and exits 1 on any difference; `--savings BEFORE` walks the corpora with a build without the grammar (`BEFORE`) and with it, and lists the commonest phrases in running text.

Writes the data the lessons site runs on, and checks every outline the lessons and reference pages teach against the built dictionary. Exits non-zero on any wrong one, and stops with "out/lyk is older than the rules: run `lyk build`" when `out/lyk/.built` is not this checkout's source hash (`--allow-stale` skips). Its output is byte-identical between runs on one `out/lyk`.
Simulates letting phrases take strokes from words.
